name: Elpaal
title: Benjaminitic clan head
summary: Elpaal was a descendant of Benjamin, the youngest son of Jacob, and is mentioned in the genealogies in 1 Chronicles. He was the son of Shaharaim and Hushim, and became the father of several sons who were leaders in the tribe of Benjamin. His descendants settled in Jerusalem and other cities and played a role in the organization of the tribe.

keyEvents.title: Elpaal's birth and lineage
keyEvents.description: Elpaal was born as the son of Shaharaim and his wife Hushim. He is recorded in Benjamin's genealogy along with his brother Abitub.

keyEvents.title: Elpaal's sons are mentioned
keyEvents.description: Elpaal's sons Eber, Misham, and Shemed are mentioned. Shemed built Ono and Lod with their surrounding towns.

keyEvents.title: Beriah and Shema as descendants
keyEvents.description: Beriah and Shema were among Elpaal's sons and became heads of families for the inhabitants of Aijalon. They drove out the inhabitants of Gath.

keyEvents.title: Elpaal's descendants in detail
keyEvents.description: An extended list of Elpaal's descendants is given in the genealogy, including Shimai, Ishmaiah, and other prominent Benjaminites.

keyEvents.title: Elpaal's place in the tribe of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: Elpaal is recorded as part of the great Benjaminite genealogy that was written down to preserve the tribe's identity, especially after the exile.
